newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian union rejects Hoogovens, UGB plan.
newsitem.headline: Belgian union rejects Hoogovens, UGB plan.

text.p: A major Belgian union said on Friday it rejected a plan by Dutch metals group Hoogovens to inject cash into Belgian steel firm Usines Gustave Boel in return for a stake in and a structuring of the Belgian firm.

FGTB spokesman Roger Leclerq told Reuters the francophone socialist trade union opposed the closure of UGB's heavy steel unit at its La Louviere plant with a loss of up to 800 jobs and demanded negotiations with management.
He also called on the Boel family, which controls UGB, to commit financially to the restructuring plan.
Hoogovens aims to inject three billion Belgian francs of fresh cash into UGB to ensure the viability of UGB's steel activities and to safeguard a remaining 1,300 jobs at its La Louviere site.
Under the deal Hoogovens will get a 50 percent stake in UGB.
Hoogovens has said it is interested in UGB's rolling mills at La Louviere and Maubeuge in northern France. The two sides agreed heavy steel production at La Louviere was uneconomical.
The UGB rolling mills will help Hoogovens overcome an imbalance between its crude steel output of some six million tonnes a year and its 4.3 million tonne rolling capacity.
